**Files analyzed:** 41 (13 modified primitives + 6 added primitives + 2 hand-authored primitives + 1 token entry point + 1 new token file + 3 new lib modules + 3 new tests + 12 surfaces)

> survive the re-skin*.

## Pattern Assignments

### `components/ui/*.tsx` — the shared primitive shape (ALL 19)

Every existing primitive follows one shape. **Any re-skin or CLI-added file that deviates is wrong.**

**Imports pattern** — `components/ui/button.tsx:1-5` (cva variant) and `components/ui/checkbox.tsx:1-7` (Radix stateful):

```tsx
import * as React from "react"
import { cva, type VariantProps } from "class-variance-authority"
import { Slot } from "radix-ui"

import { cn } from "@/lib/utils"
```

```tsx
"use client"

import * as React from "react"
import { Checkbox as CheckboxPrimitive } from "radix-ui"

import { cn } from "@/lib/utils"
import { CheckIcon } from "lucide-react"
```

Four rules visible in every file:
1. **Radix is imported from the flat `radix-ui` package as a namespace alias** (`import { Dialog as DialogPrimitive } from "radix-ui"`) — **never** `@radix-ui/react-dialog`. All of `avatar dialog dropdown-menu checkbox label button` do this. CLI-added files will match (all six declare `radix-ui` as their dep).
2. **`cn()` comes from `@/lib/utils`** (`clsx` + `twMerge`, `lib/utils.ts` is 6 lines).
3. **`"use client"` only where Radix state requires it** — `avatar checkbox dialog dropdown-menu label sonner` have it; `alert badge button card input` do NOT. Adding it needlessly to `button`/`card` would push consuming Server Components client-side (the E12 hazard).
4. **No `forwardRef` anywhere.** These are React 19 plain function components taking `React.ComponentProps<…>` and spreading `{...props}`. Do not reintroduce `forwardRef`.

**cva + data-attribute pattern** — `components/ui/button.tsx:7-65` (the canonical one to copy):

```tsx
const buttonVariants = cva(
  "group/button inline-flex shrink-0 items-center justify-center rounded-lg … focus-visible:border-ring focus-visible:ring-3 focus-visible:ring-ring/50 … disabled:pointer-events-none disabled:opacity-50 aria-invalid:border-destructive … [&_svg:not([class*='size-'])]:size-4",
  {
    variants: {
      variant: { default: "bg-primary text-primary-foreground hover:bg-primary/80", /* outline secondary ghost destructive link */ },
      size: {
        default: "h-8 gap-1.5 px-2.5 …",
        xs: "h-6 …", sm: "h-7 …", lg: "h-9 …",
        icon: "size-8", "icon-xs": "size-6", "icon-sm": "size-7", "icon-lg": "size-9",
      },
    },
    defaultVariants: { variant: "default", size: "default" },
  }
)

function Button({ className, variant = "default", size = "default", asChild = false, ...props }:
  React.ComponentProps<"button"> & VariantProps<typeof buttonVariants> & { asChild?: boolean }) {
  const Comp = asChild ? Slot.Root : "button"
  return (
    <Comp data-slot="button" data-variant={variant} data-size={size}
      className={cn(buttonVariants({ variant, size, className }))} {...props} />
  )
}

export { Button, buttonVariants }
```

**Load-bearing details in that excerpt:**
- `data-slot` on **every** rendered element (verified on all 11 files — `card` has 7 slots, `dropdown-menu` has 20). The re-skin must not drop one; they are the styling hook `radix-nova` and `shadcn/tailwind.css` key off.
- `data-variant` / `data-size` mirror the cva props onto the DOM.
- `asChild` → `Slot.Root` from `radix-ui` (not `@radix-ui/react-slot`).
- **`buttonVariants` is exported and imported by `components/ui/dialog.tsx:7`** (`import { Button } from "@/components/ui/button"`) — the Dialog close button reuses it. Changing Button's size scale changes the Dialog close affordance.
- **This is the file where the 44px floor bites hardest.** Every size is `h-6`/`h-7`/`h-8`/`h-9` and `size-6`…`size-9` — 24px to 36px. All eight are below the floor. UI-SPEC calls a token-swap treatment of this "under-scoped"; the design work is deciding whether `default` is raised to `h-11` (44px) or a phone size is added and made the default.

**Badge is the analog for the new `Tag`** — `components/ui/badge.tsx:7-49` is the same shape minus `size`, rendering a `<span>`, with `h-5 … rounded-4xl px-2 py-0.5 text-xs`. Note it applies `cn(badgeVariants({ variant }), className)` — `className` **outside** the cva call, where Button passes it **inside**. Pick one deliberately for `Tag`; `twMerge` makes them behave the same but the diff will look inconsistent otherwise.

**Radix state pattern — `components/ui/checkbox.tsx:14-29`** (the "keep `data-state` semantics" rule made concrete):

```tsx
<CheckboxPrimitive.Root
  data-slot="checkbox"
  className={cn(
    "peer relative flex size-4 shrink-0 … border border-input … after:absolute after:-inset-x-3 after:-inset-y-2 focus-visible:ring-3 … data-checked:border-primary data-checked:bg-primary data-checked:text-primary-foreground",
    className
  )}
  {...props}
>
  <CheckboxPrimitive.Indicator data-slot="checkbox-indicator" className="grid place-content-center text-current transition-none [&>svg]:size-3.5">
    <CheckIcon />
  </CheckboxPrimitive.Indicator>
</CheckboxPrimitive.Root>
```

- The state selector is **`data-checked:`** (radix-nova / Radix 1.6 shorthand), **not** `data-[state=checked]:`. `radio-group` and `switch` will arrive with the same convention — do not "normalise" it.
- `after:absolute after:-inset-x-3 after:-inset-y-2` is an **existing hit-area expander** on a `size-4` box → ~40×40px. This is the closest thing the repo has to the 44px floor and is the pattern to generalise (expand the pseudo-element, keep the visual box small) for checkbox/radio/switch rather than growing the painted control.
- `group-has-disabled/field:opacity-50` is already present — it anticipates the `field` primitive being added.

**Compound-component pattern — `components/ui/card.tsx`** (7 exports: `Card CardHeader CardTitle CardDescription CardAction CardContent CardFooter`, each `React.ComponentProps<"div">` + `data-slot`). `alert.tsx` is the same shape with cva on the root (`Alert AlertTitle AlertDescription AlertAction`), `avatar.tsx` the same with Radix (`Avatar AvatarImage AvatarFallback AvatarBadge AvatarGroup AvatarGroupCount`). **`Card` is `overflow-hidden`** — this is what made the `max-w-md` defect invisible rather than merely ugly. Do not remove it silently, and do not add `--spacing-*` keys without the width shields.

### `app/globals.css` (config, build-time transform)

**Analog: itself.** It is the single token entry point and is already structured exactly as the new layer needs.

**The `@theme inline` block already carries the four type roles** (lines 76–87) — these are the roles the imported system must collapse *into*, and they are already correct:

```css
--text-body: 16px;   --text-body--line-height: 1.5;   --text-body--font-weight: 400;
--text-label: 14px;  --text-label--line-height: 1.4;  --text-label--font-weight: 600;
--text-heading: 20px;--text-heading--line-height: 1.2;--text-heading--font-weight: 600;
--text-display: 28px;--text-display--line-height: 1.2;--text-display--font-weight: 600;
```

**The spacing scale + its width shields (lines 19–71) are the hard-constraint pattern**, with a 28-line comment explaining why:

```css
--spacing-xs: 4px; --spacing-sm: 8px; --spacing-md: 16px; --spacing-lg: 24px;
--spacing-xl: 32px; --spacing-2xl: 48px; --spacing-3xl: 64px; --spacing-touch: 44px;

/*  max-w-*  ->  --max-width  ->  --spacing  ->  --container
    `--spacing` outranks `--container` … IF YOU ADD A `--spacing-<name>` ABOVE
    and Tailwind ships a `--container-<name>`, ADD THE TWO OVERRIDES HERE TOO. */
--max-width-xs: 20rem; … --max-width-3xl: 48rem;
--min-width-xs: 20rem; … --min-width-3xl: 48rem;
```

**What must change and where:**
- Line 10–12: `--font-sans: var(--font-sans)`, `--font-mono: ui-monospace, …` hardcoded, `--font-heading: var(--font-sans)`. The three-family swap lands here (`--font-serif` is **absent today** and must be added).
- Lines 139–172 `:root` — the green `#16a34a` / zinc `#f4f4f5` palette. Every one of these is replaced by the `--cena-*` ramp. Note `--primary` AND `--ring` AND `--sidebar-primary` AND `--sidebar-ring` all carry the accent — four places, plus four more in `.dark` (lines 179–211).
- Lines 126–138 and 174–178 are **contract comments citing `01-UI-SPEC.md`** and are now factually wrong (they name `#16A34A` and "per-venue branding arrives in Phase 4 … DINER menu only", which the revised D-02 reverses). A re-skin that updates hexes but leaves these comments ships a file that documents the wrong contract.
- `@layer base` (lines 213–224): `html { @apply font-sans }`, `body { @apply … text-body }`. This is where the serif/mono family assignment hooks in.
- `@custom-variant dark (&:is(.dark *))` (line 5) — class-based, **not** `prefers-color-scheme`. This already satisfies D-10's "no `prefers-color-scheme` selector reaches a `--venue-*` token"; `token-boundary.test.ts` can assert `globals.css` and `venue.css` contain no `prefers-color-scheme` at all.

**`app/tokens/venue.css` (new)** has no analog file, but its *shape* is the `@theme inline` block above. Rule 1 of the Token Namespace Contract (`@theme inline` mandatory) is already the pattern this file uses — copy it, do not invent a `@theme` (non-inline) block.

### `app/layout.tsx` (font loading)

**Analog: itself, lines 1–13** — the only `next/font` usage in the repo:

```tsx
import { Inter } from "next/font/google";
import "./globals.css";

// UI-SPEC ## Typography: Inter via next/font/google, exposed as `font-sans`.
// Only two weights exist across the whole phase — 400 (body) and 600 …
const inter = Inter({
  variable: "--font-sans",
  subsets: ["latin", "latin-ext"],
  weight: ["400", "600"],
  display: "swap",
});

// …
<html lang="en" className={`${inter.variable} h-full antialiased`}>
```

**Copy this exactly three times** (Newsreader → `--font-serif`, Instrument Sans → `--font-sans`, IBM Plex Mono → `--font-mono`), composing all three `.variable` classes onto `<html>`. The existing call already demonstrates:
- `subsets: ["latin","latin-ext"]` — the RO/HU diacritic requirement, already right.
- `weight: ["400","600"]` — **required for IBM Plex Mono** (non-variable) per UI-SPEC; omit `weight` for the two variable families.
- `display: "swap"`.
- The `variable:` → `--font-*` → `globals.css` `@theme inline` handoff.

There is **no** `<link>` to fonts.googleapis.com anywhere in `app/` today, so SC1's font half is currently satisfied and must stay so. The `tokens/fonts.css` migration ban in UI-SPEC is what would *break* it.

### `tests/theme/*.test.ts` (new)

**Analog: `tests/lib/theme-width-scale.test.ts` — read this file before writing either new test.** It is the repo's established "assert a property of a stylesheet" idiom and UI-SPEC explicitly names its non-vacuity idiom as the one to follow.

**Read-the-stylesheet-as-data pattern** (lines 30–58):

```ts
const require = createRequire(import.meta.url);
const GLOBALS = readFileSync(new URL("../../app/globals.css", import.meta.url), "utf8");
const TAILWIND_THEME = readFileSync(require.resolve("tailwindcss/theme.css"), "utf8");

/** Every `--<namespace>-<key>: <value>;` declaration in a stylesheet. */
function declarations(css: string, namespace: string): Map<string, string> {
  const found = new Map<string, string>();
  const pattern = new RegExp(`--${namespace}-([a-z0-9]+)\\s*:\\s*([^;]+);`, "gi");
  for (const match of css.matchAll(pattern)) found.set(match[1], match[2].trim());
  return found;
}
```

`token-boundary.test.ts` should reuse `declarations()` verbatim against `app/tokens/venue.css` to assert no `--szeged-*|--napfeny-*|--paprika-*|--tisza-*` key exists.

**Non-vacuity + dynamic-table pattern** (lines 56–80) — this is the exact idiom UI-SPEC's `CONTRAST_PAIRS.length >= 8` refers to:

```ts
const collidingKeys = [...customSpacing.keys()].filter((key) => tailwindContainers.has(key)).sort();

it("still has a named spacing scale that collides with Tailwind's container scale", () => {
  expect(collidingKeys.length).toBeGreaterThan(0);
  expect(collidingKeys).toContain("md");
});

it.each(collidingKeys)("shields max-w-%s from the --spacing namespace with the container value", (key) => {
  expect(
    ourMaxWidths.get(key),
    `--max-width-${key} is missing or wrong in app/globals.css, so \`max-w-${key}\` resolves to ` +
      `--spacing-${key} (${customSpacing.get(key)}) instead of Tailwind's --container-${key} (${container}). ` +
      `That collapses every \`max-w-${key}\` shell.`,
  ).toBe(container);
});
```

Copy three things: `it.each(TABLE)` over a derived array; the **explanatory second argument to `expect()`** carrying the diagnosis (UI-SPEC requires the Annex II reference in the allergen failure message and the pair identity in the contrast failure message — this is the mechanism); and the guard test that the table is non-empty.

**Also copy the file-header comment convention.** Every structural test in this repo opens with a `/* ... */` block naming the defect it guards (see lines 5–28 here, and `unconditional-cta-coverage.test.ts` lines 7–40). The contrast test's header is where the two RESEARCH `contrast.ts` defects (unlinearised blue channel; 3-digit hex coercion) get recorded.

**Pinned values that must not move** (lines 93–108) — these are SC2's teeth:

```ts
expect(ourMaxWidths.get("sm")).toBe("24rem");
expect(ourMaxWidths.get("md")).toBe("28rem");
expect(customSpacing.get("md")).toBe("16px");
expect(customSpacing.get("touch")).toBe("44px");
```

**Consequence for the token wave:** if the migration adds any `--spacing-<k>` whose name collides with a Tailwind container name (`xs sm md lg xl 2xl…7xl`, `3xs 2xs`, `prose`), this test goes red until the matching `--max-width-<k>` and `--min-width-<k>` are added. That is the intended behaviour, not a failure to work around.

### `tests/lib/unconditional-cta-coverage.test.ts` (existing — the re-skin tripwire)

**Do not modify. Read lines 1–40 before touching `app/(dashboard)/layout.tsx`.** It parses the file with the TypeScript compiler (`import ts from "typescript"`) and **walks the ancestors** of the create-venue `<Link>` (currently at `app/(dashboard)/layout.tsx:175-181`), failing if any ancestor is a conditional. It is the analog for the **G-01-14 regression test**: a source-structural assertion over a real file path, with a header explaining the defect class ("a create/enrol CTA bound to an empty-state branch"). Its table already covers two sites (`layout.tsx` and the devices page) precisely because the defect shipped twice.

### `tests/venues/venue-form-languages.test.tsx` (existing — the G-01-13 analog)

The **G-01-13 fix must not break this file's `select.options` reads.** It is also the closest analog for the new G-01-13 regression test (a `.tsx` DOM test over `components/venue-form.tsx`). The defect site is `components/venue-form.tsx:162-167`:

```tsx
<Checkbox
  …
  disabled={enabledLanguages.length === 1 && enabledLanguages[0] === code}
/>
```

A disabled control is omitted from `FormData` → the single-language (EUR) venue submits no language. Note the file has **two native `<select>` elements (lines 137 and 181)** which UI-SPEC forbids replacing with `radix-nova/select`, and an existing comment at line 82 documenting a controlled-`<select>` workaround — the "unattended overwrite silently reverts a documented workaround" warning applies here.

### `lib/theme/contrast.ts`, `lib/format/currency.ts` (new pure utilities)

**Analogs: `lib/site-origin.ts`, `lib/venue-routes.ts`, `lib/device-cookie-policy.ts`** — the repo's existing pure-function-with-a-guard-test convention (each has a matching `tests/lib/*.test.ts`). Follow it: one module, named exports, no side effects, a co-located test in `tests/lib/` or `tests/theme/`.

## Shared Patterns

### The `cn()` merge
**Source:** `lib/utils.ts` (whole file)
**Apply to:** all 19 primitives
```ts
import { clsx, type ClassValue } from "clsx"
import { twMerge } from "tailwind-merge"
export function cn(...inputs: ClassValue[]) { return twMerge(clsx(inputs)) }
```

### Server/client split
**Source:** `app/(dashboard)/components/VenueSwitcher.tsx` (server, no `"use client"`, does the Supabase read) → `app/(dashboard)/components/venue-switcher-menu.tsx` (client, `"use client"`, holds the interaction)
**Apply to:** any surface gaining a `Tooltip`, hover state or `Tabs` during the re-skin. UI-SPEC names this pair explicitly as *the* pattern to follow. `app/(dashboard)/layout.tsx` and `components/dashboard-nav.tsx` are Server Components today and must stay so.

### Revalidation after a mutation
**Source:** `actions/staff.ts:85,114,255` and `actions/devices.ts:286`
```ts
import { revalidatePath } from "next/cache";
…
revalidatePath(`/venues/${parsed.data.venueId}/staff`);
```
**Apply to:** the **G-01-14 fix** in `actions/venues.ts`. `actions/venues.ts` is the only action file that imports `revalidatePath` nowhere (verified — grep returns no `revalidatePath` in it, only a comment at line 50 about JWT revalidation). The three sibling action files show exactly where the call goes: after the write, before the redirect.

### Lucide icon usage
**Source:** `components/ui/checkbox.tsx:7,26`, `components/ui/dialog.tsx:8`, `components/ui/dropdown-menu.tsx:7`, `components/ui/sonner.tsx:5`
```tsx
import { CheckIcon, ChevronRightIcon } from "lucide-react"
```
Named `*Icon` imports, sized by a Tailwind selector on the parent (`[&>svg]:size-3.5`, `[&_svg:not([class*='size-'])]:size-4`) rather than by props. **No `strokeWidth` is set anywhere today** — every icon renders at Lucide's stock 2. This is exactly the gap the new `components/ui/icon.tsx` wrapper closes (`strokeWidth={1.75}`), and it means **18 call sites across 18 files** must be migrated to it, not just the primitives.

### Contract comments citing the UI-SPEC
**Source:** `app/globals.css:14-18,73-75,126-138`, `app/layout.tsx:5-7`, `lib/copy.ts:1-18`
Every design-contract-bearing file carries a comment naming the UI-SPEC section it implements. The re-skin must **re-point these at `01.1-UI-SPEC.md`** — leaving them citing `01-UI-SPEC.md`'s superseded Color/Typography sections is how the next agent plans against the wrong contract.

RESEARCH § Pattern 3 supplies the reference implementation **but has two verified defects** (unlinearised blue channel; 3-digit hex silently mis-parsed) — the four oracle pins in UI-SPEC § Contrast Guardrail Contract are the contract that catches them. Do not copy the snippet as-is. |

**Command conventions for acceptance criteria** (project-established, not derivable from `package.json`):
- `pnpm exec vitest run` — there is **no** `test` script; do not write `pnpm test`
- `pnpm exec tsc --noEmit` — never `pnpm dlx tsc`
- `pnpm exec shadcn add select radio-group switch field tabs tooltip` — no `--style` flag exists
- `pnpm build` for the production build; **never `pnpm dev`** (it does not exit)
